Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3308; not anxious:--without care(-fulness), secure.
BiblicalUsage: Without care, secure, and the New Testament uses it twice for two kinds of freedom. The chief priests promise the soldiers, if this come to the governor's ears, we will persuade him, and secure you — safe from the governor, for a price. And Paul says, I would have you without carefulness, the unmarried man caring for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord; the word is the same; the security is not.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for without care carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two securities, that the priests buy safety with a lie and Paul offers freedom from care to the man who pleases the Lord.
